record.what_it_does: Cloud CRM for sales, service and marketing, with a customizable data platform.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 through an External Client App (ECA). As of Spring '26, creating new Connected Apps is restricted by default in the UI and the Metadata API, except through package installation. Re-enabling it needs a Salesforce Support request. Existing Connected Apps keep working. ECAs support Authorization Code / Web Server (with PKCE), Client Credentials, JWT Bearer and Device flows. ECAs do NOT support the Username-Password or User-Agent flows. Each customer org has its own My Domain instance URL and login endpoint. The JWT bearer flow is listed as jwt_service_account. Client credentials is an OAuth2 grant. The first pass listed 'other', but nothing beyond OAuth was confirmed, so it was removed.
record.access_notes: A free Developer Edition org gives API access for building and testing. API access is on by default in the Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer editions. Professional Edition needs the paid Web Services API add-on (the Additional API Calls product does not enable it). Users also need the 'API Enabled' permission, and orgs without API access return API_DISABLED_FOR_ORG. Customers' admins install ECAs into their orgs. AppExchange security review applies only to listing on AppExchange. Hosted MCP servers are GA for Enterprise Edition and above and included in Developer Edition. Salesforce's docs say they are intended for Flex Credits customers and that usage may be billed.
record.api_breadth_notes: REST API (sObject CRUD, describe, SOQL/SOSL query, composite), SOAP API, Bulk API 2.0, Metadata API, Tooling API, Connect REST, UI API, GraphQL API, Pub/Sub API (gRPC/HTTP2 for platform events and Change Data Capture) and the Streaming API (CometD). Hundreds of operations across all standard and custom objects. The OpenAPI 3.0 spec is a beta, generated per org for the sObjects REST API (POST /specifications/oas3), and Salesforce says not to build production integrations on it.
record.mcp_notes: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers (developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers; GitHub forcedotcom/mcp-hosted) went GA on 2026-04-29, after a beta in October 2025. They cover standard servers (sObject operations, etc.) and custom servers, with per-user OAuth 2.0 + PKCE through an External Client App. Supported clients include Claude and ChatGPT. Available in Enterprise Edition and above, and included in Developer Edition. The docs say the servers are intended for Flex Credits customers and usage may be billed. There is also the open-source local Salesforce DX MCP server (forcedotcom/mcp).
record.blocker_notes: Developer Edition orgs are free and self-serve. To serve many customers, each org's admin must install or approve the External Client App, because ECAs don't exist in a target org until they are installed. Production orgs need an API-enabled edition (Professional Edition needs a paid add-on). Do not rely on the Username-Password flow, since ECAs don't support it. Event triggers come from Change Data Capture and Platform Events through the Pub/Sub API (gRPC) or CometD streaming, and from SOAP-based Outbound Messages. These are not simple JSON webhooks.
